title: Recursive graph matching trace
statement: Let $r,k,s\in\mathbb{N}$ with $r>0$, and let $M$ be a perfect matching of the complete $2r$-partite graph whose parts each have $k$ vertices. Suppose a set $R$ of vertices has cardinality $2s$ and is closed under the matching partner map, meaning that the partner of every vertex in $R$ also lies in $R$. Then one can form a pairing trace of length $s$ on $R$: at each step, choose a pivot in a largest part of the remaining set and a partner from a different part, then continue after deleting both vertices.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a perfect matching of the complete $2r$-partite graph with $k$ vertices in each part
$R$ is closed under the matching partner map
